title: Staged exposure timeline playground notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, informal synthesis of a microstage-first canary cadence and escalation plan we can iterate with SRE/Eng/QA. This is a playground doc — not final. Trying to capture a repeatable microstage timeline, ownership handoffs, synthetic traffic checks, and clear triggers for automatic vs manual rollback.

High-level intent:
- Move away from single "canary percent" ramps toward short microstages (1m-15m) with explicit verification windows.
- Treat each microstage as a transactional unit with telemetry checklist and explicit owner.
- Optimize for fast detection + safe rollback while letting low-risk changes get fast exposure.

Definitions (for this doc):
- microstage: small duration exposure (e.g., 1m / 5m / 15m) at a defined traffic fraction.
- stage ramp: sequence of microstages to reach a target allocation.
- commit window: time after which the stage is considered stable for subsequent ramps.
- hard trigger: automated rule that immediately reverts routing (no human ok).
- soft trigger: alert & paging to oncall; human-in-loop required to revert.

Example baseline timeline (template):
- M0 (0% -> 0.5%): 1m microstage (sanity + connectivity). Owner: release steward. Checks: 3 synthetic smoke requests, token-level latency < 2x baseline.
- M1 (0.5% -> 2%): 5m microstage. Owner: release steward + SRE buddy. Checks: error rate delta < 0.5pct, latency P95 < 2x baseline, no new exceptions in error logs.
- M2 (2% -> 10%): 15m microstage. Owner: release steward. Checks: eval prompts (n=50) pass, post-gen quality heuristics (toxicity/empty-output) within thresholds.
- M3 (10% -> 50%): staggered 30m microstages (10% -> 25% -> 50%). Owner: PM + Eng oncall. Checks: production A/B metrics stable (CTR/satisfaction proxy), cost delta within budget.
- Final (50% -> 100%): slower ramp with longer observation windows and an A/B analysis day before full rollout.

Telemetry checklist (per microstage, minimal):
- Infra: pod/gpu OOMs, CPU steal, node restarts, KV cache miss spikes.
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 token and request latencies; percentage above SLO.
- Errors: 5xx rate, application exceptions, rate-limited responses.
- Quality: sampling of n outputs against eval set; automated toxicity/format checks.
- Business signals: conversion/CTR/backstop metrics (if available).
- Cost: tokens served per second + per-token unit cost variance.

Automated hard triggers (examples to implement in router):
- 3x baseline 5xx rate sustained for 60s -> immediate revert to previous route.
- New model binary failure (OOB exceptions during inference) -> immediate revert.
- P99 latency > SLO*3 sustained for 120s -> reroute.

Soft triggers (alert + page):
- Quality regression on eval-set (>4% failures) within microstage sample -> page product/quality owner.
- Cost-per-token spike > 2x expected for >10m -> page finance/infra.

Ownership & comms ritual (short):
- Preflight (T-24h): release steward posts runbook snapshot to #rollouts with expected windows and test plans. Tag: @sre-oncall, @pm.
- T-0: feature flag flips and canary schedule posted in Slack and Confluence link.
- During: release steward updates live timeline every microstage (timed messages). Use ephemeral channel: #rollout-<name>-<date>.
- Postmortem: if any trigger fired, steward files short incident note and links to telemetry snapshots.

Synthetic traffic plan (cheap but focused):
- Run n=20 deterministic evaluation prompts at M1 and M2; compare scalar metrics.
- Inject a small burst of high-seq-length requests to validate KV cache eviction behavior at M2.
- Synthetic RPS profiles: 1s spike, 10s sustained, 60s tail — check autoscaler response and latency tail.

A/B slices & measurement notes:
- For models that change quality, keep an explicit A/B for min 24 hours at >=10% exposure (if user-facing). Use pre-registered metric list (CTR, accept rate, revert-to-edit).
- Run Bayesian sequential test with prior derived from last stable baseline. Flag if posterior prob of improvement < 0.05 or prob of harm > 0.9.
- Quick sample-size lookup (rough): detect 1% absolute difference in metric with 80% power at 10% exposure -> approx 50k users (very workload-specific; run offline calculator).

Rollback paths (clear):
- Auto: router flips back to previous model (short TTL) + throttled traffic until human confirmation.
- Manual: steward triggers full rollback via the console rollback button (idempotent path documented) + stop ongoing ramps.
- Safety net: if rollback fails, route to 'fallback lightweight model' (lower-cost, well-tested) and page SRE.

Open engineering TODOs (prioritized):
1) Implement microstage timer in rollout-scheduler: support 1m/5m/15m buckets + staged commit window. (ENG: ROLL-2399)
2) Add automated quality probe runner that executes eval set during microstages and posts a delta. (ENG-2406)
3) Wire hard triggers into traffic router with immediate rollback semantics + audit log. (SRE-121)
4) Console UX: show microstage countdown, owner, and last-check results inline. (PR #67 on rollout-scheduler)

Known tradeoffs / rationales:
- Short microstages increase visibility and make rollback cheap, but add scheduling complexity and noise -> mitigated by having small, deterministic synthetic checks per stage.
- We accept more frequent human nudges early in rollout to avoid over-automation on ambiguous quality signals.

Quick checklist for the release steward (copyable):
- [ ] Post T-24 plan to #rollouts and Confluence
- [ ] Confirm SRE oncall & QA buddy assigned
- [ ] Upload microstage eval prompts and expected thresholds
- [ ] Start M0 and run smoke checks
- [ ] Document each microstage pass/fail in channel
- [ ] If any hard trigger fires, ensure rollback status posted and incident created

Unresolved questions / discussion points for next sync:
- What is the minimum microstage duration SRE will accept given autoscaler reaction times for our Dedicated customers? (estimate: 60s may be too short on slow scales)
- How to tune A/B sample size heuristics for low-traffic features — should we use stratified sampling or longer exposure?
- Do we want a separate 'quality-only' canary path that never exceeds 10% exposure but runs heavy evals? Pros/cons?

Notes to self / followups:
- Meet with Maya and Ethan to demo the synthetic probe runner week of Mar 15.
- Wire ROLL-2399 to the scheduler backlog and prioritize QA integration.

Quick links:
- Rollout scheduler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scheduler/pull/67
- Canary-observability dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/canary-summary
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SOP/Canary+Incident+Template

-- Priya
